facts.claim: BFF YAML sets a 15 minute default. Java interprets tokenExpiration in minutes.
Initial and extended access issuance add configured minutes to current epoch milliseconds.
MFE decodes exp and stores it unchanged. Home multiplies exp by 1000 and subtracts epoch milliseconds.
The inspected expiry path does not apply local timezone conversion.
The photographed access delay is 7h59m48.109s. It is below the signed 32-bit timer limit.
Refresh expiry can independently open Timeout before access expiry.
The initial login payload supplies oud and SESSION_ID. Extension removes exp and iat before access issuance.
facts.limit: The SDK applies withPayload after expiry fields. Inspected callers avoid exp and iat replacement.

private String doGenerateToken(String subject, Map<String, String> payload, Date expiresAt, String Issuer) {
        return JWT.create()
            .withIssuer(Issuer)
            .withExpiresAt(expiresAt)
            .withSubject(subject)
            .withIssuedAt(new Date())
            .withJWTId(JWT_ID)
            .withPayload(payload)

public String doGenerateTokenWithAuthTime(String subject, Map<String, String> payload) {
        return JWT.create()
            .withIssuer(JWT_ISSUER)
            .withExpiresAt(new Date(System.currentTimeMillis() + jwtConfigProperties.getTokenExpiration() * 60 * 1000))
            .withSubject(subject)
            .withIssuedAt(new Date())
            .withJWTId(JWT_ID)
            .withPayload(payload)
            .withClaim(USER_LOGIN_TIME_KEY, new Date())
            .withClaim(ABSOLUTE_IDLE, new Date(System.currentTimeMillis() + jwtConfigProperties.getAbsoluteExpiration() * 60 * 1000))
            .sign(algorithm);
